error.signature: AI tells a newcomer to Finland they can open a bank account, sign a phone contract, or register with authorities using just a passport and residence permit

verdict.summary: Finland requires a Finnish personal identity code (henkilotunnus / hetu) issued by the Digital and Population Data Services Agency (DVV) before a newcomer can open a bank account, sign most service contracts, or deal with authorities. A passport and residence permit alone are not accepted as the primary identifier. Getting a hetu requires registering with DVV (online form plus an in-person visit), and a full 'municipality of residence' registration - needed for local healthcare, benefits, and a driving licence - additionally requires an intended stay of at least one year.

dead_ends.action: Walk into a Finnish bank or telecom shop with only a passport and residence permit expecting to open an account or sign a contract the same day
dead_ends.why_fails: DVV states a Finnish personal identity code is needed 'when you contact authorities, apply for benefits or open a bank account.' Banks and telecom operators use the hetu as the primary identifier in their systems; without it the application is refused or stalls until the code is issued.
dead_ends.condition: No Finnish personal identity code yet

dead_ends.action: Assume any newcomer who registers with DVV automatically gets full 'municipality of residence' (kotikunta) status and the local services that come with it
dead_ends.why_fails: InfoFinland and DVV both specify that a municipality of residence requires an intended stay of at least one year; someone moving for less than a year (e.g. a short study or work placement) usually gets only a temporary identity code without kotikunta, and is not entitled to municipal healthcare, most benefits, or a Finnish driving licence.
dead_ends.common_misconception: That having a Finnish personal identity code by itself means you are a full local resident with access to every municipal service.

workarounds.action: Submit DVV's registration form online as soon as your grounds for residence (employment, study place, family tie, or residence permit) are confirmed, then complete the required in-person visit to DVV to receive your personal identity code
workarounds.how: DVV issues the code once your personal data and address are registered in the Population Information System; use the code from that point for banks, Kela, and employers.
workarounds.condition: Legal grounds for residence already established

workarounds.action: If your stay is under a year, register for a temporary identity code without municipality of residence, and budget for using private healthcare or your home-country coverage in the meantime
workarounds.how: A temporary code still lets you open bank accounts and pay taxes; it does not grant kotikunta-dependent municipal services, so plan health cover separately.

frequently_confused_with.distinction: This canon covers the identity code (hetu) itself; the other covers what strong-authentication tool you can use once you have one.
